text:
maria: Customer on acme-inc reported a 403 when switching projects in the console. Happens only if they switch orgs quickly (A -> B) after an SSO group mapping change. Repro steps attached below.

sam: Can you paste the minimal repro and any headers/response body?

maria: Repro: 1) Log into console as user in org A. 2) Admin updates group mapping in IdP for org B (adds user to 'prod-access'). 3) Without fully reauthing, user clicks Switch Org -> B. Console shows projects list but all actions are disabled and API calls return 403.

Example API call while console is on org B:
```
GET /api/v1/projects/123/actions
Host: console.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <browser-session-token>
Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...
```
Response: 403 Forbidden
```json
{ 
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "reason": "missing_project_access",
  "meta": {"auth_source": "sso-cache"}
}
```

maria: Browser console shows header `x-auth-refresh-required: true` in the failing responses.

alex: Sounds like the session claims cached at the auth-proxy didn't pick up the SCIM/IdP group change. The token still has old group list in the session store. Did you try forcing a session refresh?

maria: Tried sign-out/in and the UI works after that. Customer complains they need to do a full sign out every time. They want a reliable fix or a server-side fallback.

jordan: Quick workaround: call the auth refresh endpoint from the UI (POST /internal/auth/refresh-session) after org switch so token gets reloaded. Not ideal publicly but we can use it for a customer.

alex: Long-term: two fixes to consider - 1) on org switch, if `x-auth-refresh-required` is present, trigger a silent refresh flow from console (iframe / OIDC prompt=none) to exchange session cookie for updated claims; 2) reduce session TTL for claim cache or add a short-lived "group-snapshot-version" header we validate against IdP version.

maria: I ran a repro with curl to force-check the session refresh flow:
```bash
# simulate console forcing refresh after switch
curl -i -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/internal/auth/refresh-session \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"org_id":"org-b", "force":true}'
```
Return: 200 + new Set-Cookie header, subsequent project action call returns 200.

sam: Can infra patch the proxy to auto-serve a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: refresh_required` instead of 403 in these cases? That would make console run a silent reauth automatically.

deploy-bot: deploy request created: infra/auth-proxy#PM-1122 -> add auth-refresh signal header and reduce claim-cache TTL in canary region. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Filed as workaround with support: for affected customers we can 1) trigger the internal refresh endpoint from support console with customer consent, or 2) advise users to hit Sign out -> Sign in. I've added a short KB draft.

maria: I'll escalate to account team, include exact curl steps and `x-auth-refresh-required` header text. Closing here after infra confirms canary rollout. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — please paste the deploy PR once it's up so we can reference it in the KB. :eyes:
